chapter: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
title: Vernon Roulette's band at Jeffrey Tavern and Doc Cook's offer
summary: Zutty played about a year at Jeffrey Tavern in the Carroll Dickerson-style band with Earl Hines briefly on piano, until Doc Cook hired him and an altoist for Harmon's Dreamland.

bands.name: Doc Cook and His Seventeen Interns

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What were you -- who were you playing with at Jeffrey's Tavern?
I was playing with Vernon Roulette.
How do you spell that second name.
Now you see, you always get me on those things, see.
Never mind (Inaudible). Well, let's say on the --
Vernon Roulette.
Was it a TRIO ?
No, no, it was a nice band. It was Dickerson's Carroll Dickinson's band, because they had Father
Hines on piano for a while --
Oh.
Because Carrol Dickinson had just finished up a tour.
Oh, yes (unintelligible) Roulette.
Yeah. Vernon Roulette. Oh, we had a fine saxophone section and we had a real good band.
Yeah.
And since Earl Hines left, well Crowther came in, and looked like Crowther and one of the Canards daughters were married or something.
Oh, yeah.
He was formerly piano with Eddie South, they went to Europe together.
How long did this job at Jeffrey's?
Jeffrey's Tavern.
Last?
Oh, it must have lasted about a year.
A year.
Until Doc Cook came and hired Butler. Butler alto sax and myself to join his band.
Oh.
At Harmon's Dreamland.
That Harmon's Dreamland, that was the Harmon that made the Harmon mute?
Now that I really don't know.
Well, I heard that this guy did make that Harmon mute for King Oliver somewhere, and I always wondered if it was the same one, you know.
I wonder because I --
